I’ve been avoiding my delivery routes on the Westside, and I won't pull into apartment complexes or crowded gas stations anymore. I also stopped going to my basketball league and choir practice, and I completely shut down if my mom or coworkers try to ask me about that night because my chest just tightens up.\n\nDoctor: Do you find yourself constantly on the lookout for potential dangers or threats, even when you're in safe environments, like always checking for exits or watching for suspicious people?\n\nPatient: I definitely feel constantly on edge and tense all the time, like my body is always waiting for something bad to happen. But I haven't really noticed myself doing specific things like checking for exits or actively scanning the area for suspicious people.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about what you mean by feeling 'on edge' and 'tense all the time', is it more of a physical feeling, an emotional state, or a combination of both?\n\nPatient: It’s definitely a combination of both. Physically, my whole body flinches and my heart pounds at any sudden noise like a car backfiring, and I keep jerking awake in bed at night. Emotionally, I'm so wound up that the smallest things make me snap and raise my voice at people.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any difficulty falling or staying asleep, or have you been having nightmares related to the shooting?\n\nPatient: Yes, my sleep has been terrible all week. I lie in bed exhausted, but as soon as I close my eyes, I feel like I'm back in that parking lot and I toss and turn for hours. When I finally do doze off, I jerk awake at every little noise outside, terrified that someone is about to start shooting again.\n\nDoctor: Do you feel guilty or responsible in any way for what happened during the shooting, or do you blame yourself for anything related to that event?\n\nPatient: No, I don't feel responsible or guilty for the shooting itself, since I was just there delivering packages. I only feel guilty about how I've been snapping at my family and my boss lately. I know they're just trying to help, and I feel really bad about taking my stress out on them.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned feeling on edge and tense, but not specifically checking for exits or scanning for suspicious people. Have you noticed any other behaviors or thoughts that could be considered as always being 'on guard', such as an exaggerated startle response to sudden noises or an inability to relax in quiet environments?\n\nPatient: Yes, I definitely experience that. Ever since the shooting, I jump out of my skin at any sudden sound—like a car backfiring or someone dropping something loud in the warehouse. My whole body flinches, my heart starts pounding like crazy, and it takes me a really long time to calm down even after I realize there's no danger.\n\nDoctor: Have you noticed any difficulties with concentration or memory since the shooting, such as trouble focusing at work or forgetting things that you normally would remember?\n\nPatient: Yes, I'm struggling with both. I have blank spaces in my memory from that night, like I can't remember how many shots were fired or where the shooter was. On top of that, when the memories start replaying, I just freeze up and can't focus on my work or think about anything else.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned earlier that during these memory replays, you don't feel disconnected from your body, but can you tell me if there are any moments where you feel like you're in a daze or spaced out, separate from what's happening around you?\n\nPatient: No, I wouldn't say I feel like I'm in a daze or separated from my surroundings. It's more that I just feel completely frozen and locked into the memory itself when it happens.\n\nDoctor: Can you estimate how long these intrusive memories and associated symptoms have been affecting you since the shooting occurred?\n\nPatient: All of these symptoms started in the days right after the shooting in the apartment parking lot. It has been going on for about a week now.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned that these symptoms have been affecting you for about a week now, do you think they've been getting worse, staying the same, or possibly improving at all over this past week?\n\nPatient: They’ve been intense and constant ever since it happened, and it feels like things are getting harder to manage because the consequences are piling up. I feel completely on edge all the time, and the shooting is constantly replaying in my head throughout the day. It honestly feels like there is absolutely no break from it.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned the symptoms have been constant for about a week, can you confirm if you've experienced any symptom-free moments or periods where the intrusive memories and associated distress significantly decreased, even if briefly, since the shooting occurred?\n\nPatient: No, I can confirm that I haven't had any symptom-free moments at all. The scene keeps replaying in my head in a loop throughout the day, and even when a flashback slowly fades, I'm still constantly on edge and jumpy. The distress never truly goes away, so there is just no break.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned that your symptoms started right after the shooting and have been constant for about a week, but can you clarify if you've had any periods, no matter how brief, where you felt like you were back to your normal self or where the symptoms significantly decreased since the incident?"
  }
